title: Thyroid nodule: FNA, histology and the four thyroid cancers

guidelineVersions: NICE NG230 Thyroid cancer: assessment and management (December 2022)
RCPath G089 Guidance on the reporting of thyroid cytology specimens (March 2024)
RCPath G098 Dataset for the histopathological reporting of thyroid cancer (August 2023)

brief.scenario: Mrs Joanna Fairley, 45, has a 2.5 cm right thyroid nodule. She is euthyroid. The examiner will give you her ultrasound report, her fine needle aspiration cytology report and then read out the written histology findings.
brief.task: Interpret each result as it is given, including the histology findings the examiner reads out, say what happens next, and answer questions on the types of thyroid cancer.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: UK reports use Thy categories. Read each result, then say what it changes.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Treating Thy4 as a proven cancer, or as a reason to repeat the FNA and wait.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "This is Thy4, suspicious of malignancy, most likely papillary. It needs discussion at the thyroid MDT."

grid.label: Reads the FNA report
grid.fail: Treats Thy4 as a confirmed cancer or as benign, or quotes a Bethesda class without relating it to Thy.
grid.pass: Thy4: suspicious of malignancy, probably papillary; not diagnostic. Equivalent to Bethesda V.
grid.high: Gives the RCPath risk of malignancy for Thy4 (about 79%) and states all Thy4 and Thy5 cases go to the thyroid MDT.

grid.label: Next step after Thy4
grid.fail: Repeats FNA and waits, or orders an isotope scan or routine CT.
grid.pass: MDT discussion, then offer diagnostic hemithyroidectomy, or therapeutic hemithyroidectomy or total thyroidectomy.
grid.high: No routine CT or MRI for T1 to T2 disease; calcitonin only if medullary cancer is suspected. Counsels on voice, calcium and thyroxine.

grid.label: Identifies papillary carcinoma
grid.fail: Cannot name the features, or calls it follicular carcinoma because follicles are present.
grid.pass: Papillae with fibrovascular cores; crowded, clear (Orphan Annie eye) nuclei with grooves and pseudoinclusions; psammoma bodies.
grid.high: States the diagnosis rests on the nuclear features, so the follicular subtype of papillary carcinoma is still papillary.

grid.label: Stages and plans
grid.fail: Stages on size alone without the node status, or plans a preventive neck dissection.
grid.pass: 25 mm, confined to the thyroid: pT2. Hemithyroidectomy or total thyroidectomy; completion thyroidectomy if histology shows adverse features.
grid.high: No preventive neck dissection; RAI and TSH suppression follow total thyroidectomy according to risk. Papillary spreads mainly to lymph nodes.

grid.label: Follicular carcinoma
grid.fail: Says follicular carcinoma can be diagnosed on FNA.
grid.pass: Needs capsular or vascular invasion on histology, so FNA can only suggest a follicular neoplasm (Thy3f). Spreads by blood to lung and bone.
grid.high: Links Thy3f to diagnostic hemithyroidectomy, and names RAS mutations or PAX8-PPARG fusion.

grid.label: Medullary carcinoma
grid.fail: Says it arises from follicular cells, or plans thyroidectomy without excluding phaeochromocytoma.
grid.pass: Parafollicular C cells: calcitonin and CEA as markers, amyloid stroma. RET mutation; MEN2A and MEN2B.
grid.high: Germline RET testing even when it looks sporadic; exclude phaeochromocytoma before surgery; screen relatives.

grid.label: Anaplastic carcinoma
grid.fail: Books a rapidly enlarging neck mass in an older patient into routine clinic.
grid.pass: Undifferentiated, grows over weeks, threatens the airway; urgent assessment and tissue diagnosis; very poor prognosis.
grid.high: Requests rapid BRAF V600E testing because targeted therapy may be possible; involves palliative care early.

pass.text: It needs capsular or vascular invasion on histology, so FNA can only say follicular neoplasm, Thy3f. It spreads by blood to lung and bone.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Suspicious of malignancy, probably papillary. RCPath puts the risk of malignancy at about 79%, and every Thy4 goes to the thyroid MDT.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I wouldn't do routine CT or MRI for T1 or T2 disease, or measure calcitonin unless medullary is suspected. I'd counsel her on voice change, low calcium and thyroxine.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Papillary carcinoma. It's the nuclei that make the diagnosis, not the papillae, which is why the follicular subtype still counts as papillary.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: 25 mm, confined to the gland, no adverse features.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: pT2. No preventive neck dissection. Radioiodine and TSH suppression only follow total thyroidectomy, by risk. Papillary spreads mainly to nodes.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Thy3f can't separate adenoma from carcinoma, so diagnostic hemithyroidectomy answers it. RAS mutations or PAX8-PPARG fusion are typical.

high.speaker: candidate

failures.consequence: Counsels the patient wrongly; about a fifth of Thy4 nodules are benign.

failures.move: Repeating FNA and waiting after Thy4.
failures.consequence: Delays surgery that NICE recommends offering.

failures.move: Operating on medullary carcinoma without excluding phaeochromocytoma.
failures.consequence: Risks a hypertensive crisis under anaesthesia.

failures.move: Routine referral of a rapidly enlarging neck mass.
failures.consequence: Anaplastic cancer can obstruct the airway within days.

recovery.line: In the UK that maps to Thy: Bethesda V is Thy4, VI is Thy5.
I'd look at the nuclei first: clear, grooved nuclei mean papillary.

knowledge.fact: Thy1 non-diagnostic, Thy2 non-neoplastic, Thy3a atypia, Thy3f follicular neoplasm, Thy4 suspicious, Thy5 malignant.
Thy4 and Thy5: offer diagnostic hemithyroidectomy, or therapeutic hemithyroidectomy or total thyroidectomy.
Papillary is the most frequent type; BRAF V600E is its most frequent mutation.
Follicular carcinoma needs capsular or vascular invasion on histology.
NIFTP: non-invasive, extremely low risk, not overtly malignant; treated by lobectomy alone.
Medullary: germline RET testing for all.

recall.think: Airway (anaplastic) and phaeochromocytoma (medullary) are what can kill.
recall.say: "Thy4, suspicious of papillary carcinoma: thyroid MDT."
do: Map Thy to the NICE table
recall.trap: Thinking FNA can diagnose follicular carcinoma.
recall.finish: Hemithyroidectomy or total thyroidectomy; completion if histology demands.

partner.opening: Mrs Fairley's ultrasound shows a 2.5 cm solid, hypoechoic right nodule with microcalcification and no abnormal nodes. Her FNA report says Thy4. Interpret it.

reveals.trigger: Candidate interprets the FNA and asks for more
reveals.finding: Cytology comment: 'Cells with nuclear grooves and occasional intranuclear pseudoinclusions; suspicious of papillary carcinoma.'

She has a right hemithyroidectomy. Read out: the H&E section of the nodule shows branching finger-like fronds, each with a central core of connective tissue and thin-walled vessels, with some areas forming small follicles. The lining cells have enlarged, crowded, overlapping nuclei with pale, empty-looking centres, longitudinal grooves and occasional round pink inclusions within the nucleus. Scattered small, round, concentrically laminated purple calcified bodies lie in the cores.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks for the histology report
reveals.finding: Classic papillary carcinoma, 25 mm, confined to the thyroid, no vascular invasion, margins clear.

Read out, from a different patient: the H&E section of a thyroid tumour shows nests and sheets of polygonal and spindle-shaped cells with finely granular cytoplasm and fairly uniform round to oval nuclei. The nests are separated by pale pink, acellular, amorphous material in the stroma. No papillae or colloid-filled follicles are seen.

push.question: What does Thy4 mean, and what is its Bethesda equivalent?
push.expect: Suspicious of malignancy; Bethesda V; not diagnostic.

push.question: What would you offer her?
push.expect: MDT; diagnostic hemithyroidectomy, or therapeutic hemithyroidectomy or total thyroidectomy.

push.question: Stage this tumour and tell me if she needs more surgery.
push.expect: pT2; completion only if adverse features.

push.question: Why can't FNA diagnose follicular carcinoma?
push.expect: Needs capsular or vascular invasion, seen only on histology.

push.question: What must you do before operating on medullary carcinoma?

curveballs.prompt: The final histology says NIFTP. Is that a cancer?
curveballs.safeAnswer: No. It is a non-invasive neoplasm with extremely low risk, not overtly malignant; lobectomy alone is enough.
Not routinely: only if medullary carcinoma is suspected, for example family history or suggestive ultrasound.
That is malignant, the equivalent of Thy5; MDT and surgery.
